questions.evidence: P1 scores 79.30 vs old v0.5 73.10 under repaired policy. P1 has stronger evidence quality, lower overhead, and comparable product quality. P1 is the better candidate.

P1 composite score 79.30 beats Vanilla 65.75 due to process/evidence/overhead dimensions. But Vanilla has higher pure product quality (85 vs 84). P1's composite win comes from process infrastructure, not product superiority.
questions.nuance: Vanilla wins on product-only comparison (85 vs 84). P1 wins on composite. The 1-point product gap is negligible.

questions.q: Does P1 show product benefit, process benefit, both, or neither?
questions.evidence: Product quality is comparable across runs (Vanilla 85, P1 84, old v0.5 82). P1's advantage is process quality (80 vs 78/55/40) and evidence quality (82 vs 70/55/45). P1 adds verifiability without degrading product.

questions.q: Should multi-agent remain not-default, become conditional, or proceed?
questions.evidence: P1 shows process benefit but not product benefit on this benchmark. Multi-agent should be CONDITIONAL: used when process/evidence quality matters more than minimal overhead, NOT when pure product speed is the goal.
conditions: Use when evidence quality is important (auditable systems)
Use when team coordination benefit outweighs agent overhead
Not recommended for small projects (<500 LOC) where single agent is sufficient
Requires P1 runtime gates (reviewer, floor checks, overhead budget)

questions.q: Did policy repair change interpretation of AGENT-8-P1/R1?
questions.evidence: Under old policy, P1 was BLOCKED_BY_REVIEWER with 2 unmet floors. Under repaired policy, P1 meets all 11 hard floors. The BLOCKED_BY_REVIEWER was a policy artifact, not a product deficit. AGENT-5-P1 repair correctly identified and fixed the policy defect.
